input.job: I am an office coordinator for an office of about 70 people. I prepare and organize lunch for everyone. I order drinks, restock the fridges and keep the office clean and organized. I take care of the plants and general maintenance. I handle special orders and preparations for company events. I coordinate suppliers and make sure we have what we need. I am the person everyone comes to when something is missing or needs fixing. If the printer runs out of ink I find a replacement, and if we have none I order more.

qas.title: What do you do over and over, every day or every week?
Which would save you the most time if it got easier?
How often do you do this?
Do you work on a phone, a computer or both?
Can you use AI for your work?
Would your company let you link your work email to an AI tool?

design.read: From now on, people enter their own lunch choice in one form, so you no longer collect orders by email, on paper or in person. The form's results page counts each choice for you, and you send the caterer one email with those counts. Each week you clear the old answers and send the same link again.

steps.say: Create the form. Tally has written the questions for you.
Send the form link to everyone in your message.
On order day, open the answers in Forms. The count for each choice is already there.
Save the order email once, so each week you only fill in the blanks.
Open your saved email, fill in the counts from the results page, read it through and send it to the caterer.
After you order, clear last week's answers so the form is ready for the next round.

design.good: Everyone answers in the form, the counts on the results page add up to the number of people ordering, and the caterer confirms the order you sent.
design.approval: Before you send the email, check that the counts match the results page, the day and time are right, and any vegetarian or gluten free orders are included.

design.read: Your fridge restock now runs from one Excel list. You type what is in the fridges, the list shows what is below your usual amount, and you send one email to the supplier from a saved draft. This replaces looking and counting every item in your head, and you only order what the list shows.

material.label: Your fridge restock list
items: Item | In the fridge now | Usual amount

material.label: Your fridge restock order
items: Subject: Fridge restock order for [delivery day]

Hello [supplier name],

I would like to place our fridge restock order for [delivery day].

Item and amount:
[item 1] x[amount]
[item 2] x[amount]
[item 3] x[amount]

Please confirm the order and the delivery time. Let me know if anything is not available.

Thank you,
[your name]

material.label: Your reminder title
items: Check the fridges and send the restock order

steps.say: Create an Excel sheet with the three columns and the items Tally wrote. Fill in the usual amounts where you see brackets.
Add the list that shows what is below its usual amount, with the amount to order beside it.
Save the order email so it is ready to reuse.
Set a daily reminder to check the fridges.
Each day, type what is in the fridges now beside each item. The low list updates by itself.
Open your saved email as a new draft, copy the low items and amounts into it, read it through and send it. The next day you simply update the counts again.

design.tryOn: This week's fridge check, starting with the drinks.
design.good: You count once, the list shows only what is low, and one email goes to the supplier with the right amounts.
design.approval: Check the amounts against what you see in the fridges, and read the email and the supplier name before you send it.
